sections.h2: Selling options for a Richardson owner
sections.html:
In Richardson the realistic choices are an agent listing, a do-it-yourself sale, and a direct as-is purchase. A listing rewards a house in strong condition. The as-is route suits someone who wants no repairs, no showings and no long wait.

Richardson lies partly in Dallas County and partly in Collin County, and the line affects tax bills and school boundaries alike. Before choosing, find out three things: your county, your school district and your loan balance. Together they set your floor and your timeline.

  • Listing: wide exposure, then inspection requests and loan approval on someone else's schedule.
  • Private sale: you save the commission and do the contract and buyer screening yourself.
  • As-is purchase: no repair list, and you bargain over the closing date.

sections.h2: Where to pay the county tax bill
sections.html:
The county, not the city, collects your property tax bill. Pay at the tax office for the county your address falls in.

On the Dallas side, the appraisal district serves 61 local governing bodies. Collin CAD handles the other side and posts rates on a taxing-entities page. To contest a value, ask the appraiser for an informal review before the hearing date.

Richardson will pay a homeowner who spends heavily on remodeling a single-family house. The payment equals ten times the increase in city taxes that results from the higher appraised value.

  • The project must cost at least $20,000 and finish within 24 months of approval.
  • Apply to Community Services before construction starts, and agree to inspections.
  • The appraisal district's certified value decides the tax increase.
  • Owners delinquent on taxes or fees are not eligible.

Payment comes on April 1 of the first full calendar year after the work is done, under an economic development agreement. Reach Community Services at the Temporary City Hall Annex on Campbell Creek Blvd, 972-744-4166. The payment may count as taxable income. A remodel will not pay you back before a sale, but an owner who stays can benefit.

Richardson ISD covers 46 square miles in Dallas County, with more than 36,000 students on 50 campuses. Plano ISD serves the northern parts of Richardson on the Collin County side. Families often search by school zone, so put the district in your listing.

sections.h2: Commuting and amenities buyers ask about
sections.html:
Rail access is a selling point here. The city's pages describe DART rail and bus service, the Trinity Railway Express and NTTA tollways, and it lists hike and bike trails plus a transportation and mobility department. A commuter will want to know how far the house sits from a station, so measure the walk before you list.

Public amenities also give you something specific to name in an ad: the Eisemann Center, Sherrill Park Golf Course, a senior center, a tennis center, a gymnastics center and the recreation centers. The city sends a Richardson Today newsletter and runs a MyRichardson app for reporting issues, so buyers who follow city news will see a city that communicates often.

If a tenant still lives in the house, tell buyers about the lease up front and expect questions about showing times.

sections.h2: City services and permits to check before a sale
sections.html:
The city site lists code enforcement, residential building inspection with online permits, floodplain information, a 24/7 response center, trash and brush pickup, and permits for garage sales and alarms. A buyer's inspector may raise any of them.

  • Confirm permits for any addition or remodel through building inspection.
  • Look up the floodplain information for your address.
  • Pay or close out water service through the water customer service page.
  • Ask about brush and bulky item collection before you clear out a house.

Richardson also keeps a winter water conservation plan: residents may water at any time on their designated watering days. Expect the city to hold homes to its codes.

sections.h2: Property taxes and exemptions at a Richardson closing
sections.html:
Since the lien took hold on January 1, the title company at closing divides that year's bill between you and the buyer. Bills go out around October 1, and January 31 is the usual cutoff.

From February 1, penalty and interest build, and by July the penalty reaches 12 percent. Homeowners who are over 65 or disabled can use installment plans. School districts must grant a $140,000 homestead exemption, and a homestead's appraised value may rise no more than 10 percent a year.

A buyer may have to apply for their own exemption, so find out from the appraisal district what is on your account.

sections.h2: Preparing a Richardson house for showings
sections.html:
Tour your own house the way a city inspector would. Look for unpermitted additions, floodplain questions and yard issues that code enforcement could flag. A short list of repairs finished before photos beats a long list of credits negotiated later.

Keep permit records, the water account number and your school district's name on hand for quick answers. Buyers in a two-county city often ask which county bills the taxes, so know the answer for your parcel.

When a Texas loan goes into default, the lender may auction the house with no lawsuit. A borrower gets 20 days after the default letter to catch up, and the lender must mail the sale notice at least three weeks ahead of the auction, held on a first Tuesday.

An inherited house follows a route set by the estate. A will may go to probate any time in the four years after death. A modest estate, $75,000 or less excluding the homestead, can use a small estate affidavit with a judge's approval. A bare affidavit of heirship is merely a sworn statement, and buyers may refuse it. If the owner signed a beneficiary deed, the heir records proof of death before selling.

The clerk of whichever county covers the parcel handles recording. The state clerk manual sets the per-page charge and other records fees.

sections.h2: What a Richardson closing looks like
sections.html:
After you accept an offer, the title company starts a title search and requests a balance from the county tax office. It also requests a payoff from your lender. If your address is in Dallas County, call 214-653-7811. For Collin County, call 972-881-3014.

Closing is mostly signing. You sign the deed, the title company settles your loan and any tax due, and you keep the balance. A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, so timing hinges mainly on clearing title. Before you hand over keys, close your water account through the city and take a last reading.

If you plan a remodel before selling, remember that the incentive program pays only after the work is finished and a full calendar year has begun, so it will not help a quick sale.

faqs.q: Do I pay Richardson property tax to the city?
faqs.a: Taxes are paid at the county tax office where the property sits, so use the Dallas or Collin County office for your address.

faqs.q: Is Richardson in Dallas County or Collin County?
faqs.a: Yes, both. Each county's tax office serves part of the city.

faqs.q: How big must a project be for the Home Improvement Incentive Program?
faqs.a: At least $20,000, completed within 24 months of approval, with an application filed before construction starts.
Richardson ISD and Plano ISD. Richardson ISD spans 46 square miles in Dallas County, and Plano ISD covers northern parts of the city.

faqs.q: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Unpaid bills turn delinquent on February 1, after the January 31 cutoff, and penalty and interest begin.
